challenge.better_approach: Considered: (a) the orchestrator's first key, ticket bytes plus named proofs' seal fingerprints, rejected by measurement: _walk_bindings parses 6880 modules transitively and _added_by_the_build reads working-copy writes_to files, both outside the seal's directory_fingerprint, so that key serves stale verdicts; (b) speeding up _walk_bindings with a per-run AST cache, which helps (28.5 s of 107.5 is ast.parse) but still re-judges all 1033 every inspect; (c) a hand-listed input set per sieve, rejected because a read the list forgets is a silent green, which is why the recorder is the audit hook. The recorded-inputs cache is the build-system answer (make/bazel record what a step read) and the smallest one that is sound.
challenge.hidden_assumption: That lacks() is a function of the files it opens, the paths it finds absent, its git reads and its crossings: no clock, no environment variable, no network. To measure at /sorted: grep proof_coverage.py for time/datetime/os.environ reads inside lacks' call tree. And that sys.addaudithook 'open' sees every Python-level open (it does for open(), io.open, Path.read_text; it does not see stat, hence the separate absence wrapper).
challenge.prior_art: In house: crossings._index caches on (path, mtime, size) of every journal (the stat is the invalidation), and 7bdcd8a801df pins its listing; validation_store.source_fingerprint is the seal's closure hash. Field: content-addressed build caches (bazel action cache, ccache) key on every input read. Nothing in the congruency lab caches a sieve's judgement.
challenge.real_collision: None exclusive. 7bdcd8a801df's bounds put this out of its scope as a sibling. Law 6: the cache is the holder's (codemother) state under tools/proof_coverage/0/, not proof_coverage's own, so the tool still has no state of its own address. RULE 1: build_inspector passes the berth path in; proof_coverage never reaches into codemother.

answers.falsifier: (1) a warm run over the house tree returns findings identical to a cold run, and is faster; (2) flipping one byte of the ticket, of a named proof's seal, of a module the proof binds two hops away, and of a decompose writes_to file each re-judges exactly that ticket and no other; (3) deleting a recorded input, or creating a file the run recorded absent, re-judges; (4) a ref recorded at one sha that resolves to another re-judges; (5) under sys.addaudithook('open') every file lacks() opens is in the recorded set. WRONG INTENT if the warm/cold findings differ on an unchanged tree (the cache is serving something lacks() would not say).
answers.from_idea: none, because this is a measured cost, not an idea: /tmp/claude-1000/-home-akien-dev-src-cairn/0b2e196e-7177-4140-8585-e9f2200689b4/scratchpad/prof_lacks.out records proof_covers_the_ticket at 107.5 s over 1033 proof_coverage.lacks() calls under the 7bdcd8a801df pin, and the orchestrator queued the cache as the sibling 7bdcd8a801df's bounds name ('the PROVED re-judge (a sibling ticket)')
answers.how: proof_coverage.lacks gains a recorded-inputs cache. One judgement runs under a recorder: a sys.addaudithook 'open' hook, scoped by a flag to that one call, records every file opened with (mtime_ns, size, sha256); a wrapper over proof_coverage's own existence checks (Path.is_file / exists in _walk_bindings, _module_file, _added_by_the_build) records every path found ABSENT; every git read is recorded as the resolved commit sha plus the command (git show <sha>:<rel> needs no rehash; a ref that resolves to a new sha is a miss); the ticket's crossings entries and the decompose berth path ride the record. A hit is: ticket bytes equal, every recorded file re-stats equal (an mtime/size change falls through to sha256), every absent path still absent, every ref resolves to the recorded sha. The record berths as tool state under its holder, ~/.cairn/devices/codemother/0/tools/proof_coverage/0/lacks_cache.json (Law 6), passed in by proof_covers_the_ticket; no cache argument means today's uncached behaviour.
answers.traces_to: Law 1 (the resolver is spent on the novel, not on re-deriving the settled): 1033 judgements re-derived on every inspect though almost none of their inputs moved. Law 8/9 bound the shortcut: a cache that serves green over a moved input is a hollow green, so the record is every input read, measured by an audit hook, not a hand list.
answers.what: build_inspector's PROVED re-judge (proof_covers_the_ticket) re-runs proof_coverage.lacks() for a ticket only when an input that judgement read has changed, so an unchanged ticket is answered from the record of its last judgement and an inspect() spends the resolver only on what moved.

bullets.text: Under the 7bdc pin the PROVED re-judge is 107.5 s, not 246: 76 s of it is proof_binds_its_subject_at_call parsing 6880 modules transitively, 24.5 s is _added_by_the_build's git show per writes_to file.
A seal-fingerprint key would serve stale greens: the modules a proof binds and the build's writes_to files are read by lacks() and sit outside the seal's closure fingerprint.
